newsitem.title: USA: U.S. needs emerging markets trade focus -- Garten.
newsitem.headline: U.S. needs emerging markets trade focus -- Garten.

text.p: The United States should make international trade the leading edge of its foreign policy regarding emerging markets, Jeffrey Garten, President Clinton's former undersecretary of commerce for international trade, told Reuters.
"Unless we engage these countries in more and more trade and investment, we're not going to have influence in other areas," said Garten, who is now dean of the Yale School of Management.
Garten said the United States should make trade a top priority even with countries it has human rights qualms with, such as China.
He urged U.S. trade officials to pressure China to open all sectors of its economy to U.S. investment, but he said threatening to cut off Chinese imports would be a mistake.
"The products the Chinese are selling to us are low-cost and they're very good. We can't cut off imports without hurting our own consumers," Garten said.

Asked about regional bodies such as the Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA), and Latin American customs group Mercosur, Garten said they did not necessarily conflict with U.S. initiatives such as NAFTA (North American Free Trade Agreement).
"I don't think there has to be a conflict. The regional arrangement can be made to be building blocks to even bigger ones," he said.
But Garten said the United States must press for trade arrangements with emerging economies before they become "submerged" under the authority of other nations.
For example, Poland could become more closely aligned with the European Union and Indonesia could flip into the influence of Japan, he said.
Garten was at the Philip Morris International headquarters here to present his new book, "The Big Ten: The Big Emerging Markets and How They Will Change Our Lives."
He said the 10 countries to focus on are Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, China, India, Indonesia, South Korea, Poland, Turkey and South Africa.
Asked why Russia was not among the group, Garten said, "I didn't put Russia in there because the countries had to have taken some credible steps toward economic reform."
"It's a mafia-dominated economy right now," he said.
Later, during his presentation, Garten said the United States is poorly prepared to deal with the rise of these "big emerging markets."
He said the United States needed to develop domestic economic policies to better position itself on the changing global landscape.
"I don't think the country is focused on this at all," he said.
Garten's presentation was sponsored by the Forum for World Affairs and Philip Morris International.
